title: His Colleague Secretly Drugged Him. Nine Days Later, He Was Dead.
description:
In 1953, the CIA secretly drugged an Army scientist with LSD as part of a classified mind-control program. Nine days later, he was dead -- and it took decades for even part of the truth to come out.

The full story -- the cover-up, the destroyed evidence, and who else this program touched -- is linked below.

sources: Contemporary reporting on the 1975 Ford administration apology and settlement

scenes.text: In 1953, the CIA started secretly testing mind control on American citizens -- without their knowledge or consent.
One of them was Frank Olson, an Army scientist. At a work retreat in November of that year, his own colleague secretly spiked his drink with LSD, as part of a classified experiment.
Nobody told him what had happened. Over the next several days, he spiraled -- disoriented, paranoid, unable to explain what was wrong with him.
Nine days later, Frank Olson fell to his death from the 13th floor of a New York hotel room.
The government called it suicide. Then something else. What actually happened in that room has never been fully settled.
And Frank Olson wasn't the only person this program touched. The full story -- the cover-up, the destroyed files, and who else it connects to -- is linked in the description below.
